subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a male Drow apostate with no noble house affiliation and no apparent strategic value, yet was the subject of a costly contract to protect him from Ilvara's House and the T'sarran goons.
source_quote: You don't belong to any noble house, your background is a complete mystery, you suddenly show up, and all of a sudden, we're contracted to protect a nobody.

subject: Nym
fact: Nym is a Drow mercenary who speaks with the tone of Menzoberranzan’s natural courtesy, dismisses threats with elegant indifference, and states that the contract terms were to prevent other drow factions from killing Daz.
source_quote: Our terms of our contract were to make sure that the other drow factions didn't get you killed.

subject: Kaelira
fact: Kaelira is a Drow mercenary who expresses professional puzzlement at the scale of expenditure on Daz’s protection, noting that his lack of lineage makes the payment inexplicable.
source_quote: That is an excellent question. You don't belong to any noble house, your background is a complete mystery, you suddenly show up, and all of a sudden, we're contracted to protect a nobody. Do you know how much money that required us to get, for us to do? A lot. Like, they interrupt you. A lot.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is the Drow city where contracts for protection are issued, noble houses wield influence, and financial insulation around payments indicates the payer seeks to avoid association due to embarrassment, illegality, or danger.
source_quote: In Menzoberranzan, that level of insulation around a financial transaction means exactly one thing: the payer has significant reason not to be associated with the purchase.

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: House Mizzrym is one of the two named drow houses that sought to kill Daz, as referenced in the contract terms and threat assessment.
source_quote: House Mizzrym. House T'sarran. Those were the parameters.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran is one of the two named drow houses that sought to kill Daz, and the mercenaries were prepared to handle them personally if necessary.
source_quote: House Mizzrym. House T'sarran. Those were the parameters. They'd been prepared to handle the T'sarran contingent personally if it came to that.

subject: Ilvara's House
fact: Ilvara's House is a drow faction that Daz was contracted to be protected from, and is referenced as a threat by the mercenaries.
source_quote: Hired to protect me — specifically, me — from Ilvara's House and from the T'sarran goons we'd just finished burning.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a Lolth cultist who declared herself in charge after surviving chaos, and was killed by Zalthir with the Eldritch Claw Tattoo after a failed grapple by Thorin.
source_quote: I am blessed by Lolth!... I stepped in. The Eldritch Claw Tattoo doesn't announce itself... Asha Vandree did not get another word out.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a Drow who made the decisive call to kill Asha Vandree using the Eldritch Claw Tattoo, believing someone had to act when others hesitated.
source_quote: I'm making a call... I stepped in... Someone had to make the call. I made it. That's all.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin attempted to subdue Asha Vandree with a grapple and hand over her mouth, but was corrected by Nym for failing to kill a Lolth cleric properly.
source_quote: I also put my hand across her mouth so she can't talk, so... When attacking a cleric of Lolth, one does not just simply grapple them.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum attempted to use divine light against Asha Vandree but missed, and later expressed a preference for non-lethal solutions.
source_quote: He leveled something at her — a directed burst of divine light that should have taken her off her feet — and it missed... I would prefer not to kill anyone and was trying very hard to think of an alternative.

subject: the extraction contract
fact: The extraction contract is a document produced by the party that was at the center of the threat assessment, later referenced by Kaelira as having been scorched and significant.
source_quote: Kaelira gestured toward the scorched remnants of the extraction contract the party had produced — the document that had apparently been at the center of all this.

subject: the killing of Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree was killed by Zalthir using the Eldritch Claw Tattoo after a failed attempt to grapple her, resulting in a silence that followed a decision that could not be walked back.
source_quote: I stepped in... Asha Vandree did not get another word out. The silence after was the particular kind that follows a decision you can't walk back.

subject: the negotiation of Daz’s protection contract
fact: Daz’s protection was contracted by an anonymous payer in Menzoberranzan, with the mercenaries unaware of the employer’s identity, and the payment amount described as extraordinary.
source_quote: Someone had paid for this. Someone who knew I was here, knew who was hunting me, and knew enough to contract professionals rather than handle it directly. A lot. Like, they interrupt you. A lot.

subject: the departure of the Drow sisters
fact: Nym and Kaelira departed after fulfilling the contract, professionally and without ceremony, indicating the transaction was complete and no further obligation existed.
source_quote: The sisters departed. Professionally. Without ceremony. The contract was fulfilled; they were done.

subject: the Garden Shadow
fact: The Garden Shadow is a place associated with teachings on social authority, referenced by Zalthir in his analysis of Asha Vandree’s claim to leadership.
source_quote: I've read rooms like this before. The Garden Shadow had a saying — or possibly Brother Quellin did... that the most dangerous person in a room isn't the one with the blade drawn. It's the one who has already decided they've won.

subject: the Eldritch Claw Tattoo
fact: The Eldritch Claw Tattoo is a magical ability used by Zalthir to execute Asha Vandree with precise, non-verbal strikes that prevented her from speaking or casting.
source_quote: The Eldritch Claw Tattoo doesn't announce itself... my hands were something else — longer, reaching — and the strikes came in sequence...

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel is a halfling whose book contains the phrase 'standing at the edge of the question that changes everything,' which the narrator associates with his current existential state.
source_quote: Milo Goodbarrel, that relentlessly hopeful halfling whose book I'd read too many times to admit, had a phrase for the sensation I was experiencing. He called it 'standing at the edge of the question that changes everything.'

subject: the revelation of Daz’s unknown value
fact: Daz realizes that his survival has been funded at great cost by an unknown party in Menzoberranzan, and that his lack of status makes the investment inexplicable — suggesting hidden significance.
source_quote: I literally have no idea why there's all this focus on me... Someone in Menzoberranzan had spent generously — they interrupt you, a lot — to ensure that a male Drow apostate with no house affiliation and no apparent strategic value survived.

subject: the monastery’s combat drills
fact: The monastery’s combat drills are referenced by Zalthir as the source of the precision used in the Eldritch Claw Tattoo strikes against Asha Vandree.
source_quote: the strikes came in sequence, each one placed with the kind of precision that the monastery's combat drills were actually good for, the part of the curriculum I had paid attention to.

subject: Brother Harren
fact: Brother Harren is a former instructor at the monastery who taught a class on decisive action under moral uncertainty, which Zalthir recalls but cannot remember the content of.
source_quote: There was a class for this. Decisive action under moral uncertainty — the ethics of necessary violence, or something like that. I think it was Brother Harren, the one who never sat down, who taught it. I don't remember what he said.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree was a cleric of Lolth who had also become, in some capacity, a cleric of Zuggtmoy, and in the end she had been indistinguishable from the rot she served.
source_quote: Asha Vandree had been a cleric of Lolth who had also become, in some capacity, a cleric of Zuggtmoy, and in the end she had been indistinguishable from the rot she served.

subject: holy symbol of Lolth
fact: Asha Vandree possessed a holy symbol of Lolth.
source_quote: The holy symbol of Lolth.

subject: chain mail
fact: Asha Vandree wore chain mail.
source_quote: Chain mail.

subject: prayer beads
fact: Asha Vandree carried prayer beads.
source_quote: Prayer beads.

subject: sealed wax pouch
fact: Asha Vandree carried a sealed wax pouch.
source_quote: And a sealed wax pouch.

subject: Drow cloak
fact: Asha Vandree wore a Drow cloak of fine spider-silk that drinks shadow.
source_quote: Zalthir took the Drow cloak she'd been wearing — the fine spider-silk kind that drinks shadow.

subject: wax pouch contents
fact: The sealed wax pouch contained pages of close, careful script — the handwriting of someone who had once been methodical, who had trained as a theologian and brought that training to bear on a question that should not have been asked.
source_quote: Inside were pages of close, careful script — the handwriting of someone who had once been methodical, who had trained as a theologian and brought that training to bear on a question that should not have been asked.

subject: theological text
fact: The wax pouch contained a theological exploration claiming that Zuggtmoy and Lolth are the same thing.
source_quote: It's basically a long theological exploration of why Zuggtmoy and Lolth — and claiming that Lolth and Zuggtmoy are the same thing.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara was a high priestess of Lolth who had been actively subverted by Zuggtmoy.
source_quote: Ilvara was a high priestess of Lolth who had been actively subverted by Zuggtmoy.

subject: Ilvara's prayer book
fact: Ilvara's prayer book was a standard Lolth devotional text with marginalia in a different hand, documenting her corruption timeline.
source_quote: The main text was a standard Lolth prayer book — the kind of thing they give to promising young acolytes in the outer sanctums of any major drow religious house. The marginalia told the story. A different hand. That detail mattered to me more than any of the specific words.

subject: Ilvara's marginalia
fact: The marginalia in Ilvara's prayer book showed a gradual shift from formal prayer to associative, unstructured writing, indicating psychological corruption.
source_quote: Then, gradually, around the margins, a second voice crept in. Less structured. More associative. The sentences didn't always end. Some of them were questions that answered themselves with other questions.

subject: sealed orders from House Mizzrym
fact: The sealed orders from House Mizzrym were frantic inquiries demanding Ilvara's location and activities after her disappearance.
source_quote: Where are you? What have you been doing? Respond — kind of thing. You've gone missing. Followed by more frantic: where are you, where are you? Didn't you read the previous memo? What's up?

subject: letter from Neverlight Grove
fact: The letter from Neverlight Grove recorded a missed political meeting, indicating Ilvara’s allegiance had shifted beyond diplomatic reach.
source_quote: A missed meeting. Political correspondence that had gone nowhere, because the person it was addressed to had gone somewhere else — somewhere a Demon Queen's influence had been a stronger pull than any political alliance.

subject: Living Serpent Head Scourge
fact: The Living Serpent Head Scourge was a scourge whose head was an actual living serpent, or had been, in some intermediate state between alive and not.
source_quote: The Living Serpent Head Scourge sounds... it sounds like a great museum piece. A scourge whose head was an actual living serpent, or had been, in some intermediate state between alive and not.

subject: water-damaged prisoner journal
fact: A water-damaged journal from a prisoner who had written things down and then presumably stopped being able to, with swollen pages, run ink, and visible handwriting in drier sections.
source_quote: We also found a water-damaged journal from a prisoner we would never meet — someone who had written things down and then, presumably, stopped being able to. I held it carefully. The pages were swollen and the ink had run in places, but the handwriting was still visible in the drier sections, the marks of a person who had kept records right up until they couldn't.

subject: flask of Overbright brandy
fact: A flask of Overbright brandy was received with considerable personal interest.
source_quote: The flask of Overbright brandy I received with considerably more personal interest.

subject: confiscated prisoner belongings
fact: Confiscated prisoner belongings included Thorin’s tooth, which Ilvara had carried as a trophy.
source_quote: Confiscated prisoner belongings. Ilvara had been carrying it. Of course she had — she was exactly the sort of high priestess who would keep trophies, who would drag along evidence of her ownership of people... I opened it, and the contents were exactly what you would expect... 'like your tooth, Thorin.'... He reached in and found it. He held it for a moment without saying anything.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin’s tooth had been taken and carried by Ilvara as a trophy of ownership.
source_quote: 'like your tooth, Thorin.'... Oh, yeah. I want my tooth back.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir took the Drow cloak from Asha Vandree’s body.
source_quote: Zalthir took the Drow cloak she'd been wearing — the fine spider-silk kind that drinks shadow.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was cataloguing the room and paying close attention to implications of recovered items.
source_quote: Daz looked over from where he was already cataloguing the rest of the room. Daz was paying attention in the way he pays attention to things — still, cataloguing, already working the implications.

subject: Gorg'Bahamut
fact: Gorg'Bahamut was the narrator's mentor, who would have wanted a pious ritual performed over the dead.
source_quote: My mentor Gorg'Bahamut would have wanted me to.

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud sat down across from Protanther after four hundred years of preparation and still had a blind spot.
source_quote: I thought, briefly, of Stroud sitting down across from Protanther. Four hundred years of preparation. Still had a blind spot.

subject: Protanther
fact: Protanther was the subject of Stroud’s long preparation and eventual blind spot.
source_quote: I thought, briefly, of Stroud sitting down across from Protanther. Four hundred years of preparation. Still had a blind spot.

subject: Tongued merchant
fact: A merchant once known to the narrator had been Tongued by a bardic curse, producing correspondence eerily similar to Ilvara’s marginalia.
source_quote: I had seen something like this before, in a completely different context — a merchant I once knew who had been Tongued by a bardic curse, whose correspondence from that period was eerily similar.

subject: Underdark
fact: Ilvara had been carrying Thorin’s tooth around the Underdark.
source_quote: she had been carrying his tooth around the Underdark.

subject: prayer book marginalia
fact: The marginalia in Ilvara’s prayer book showed a corruption timeline, beginning with formal prayer and evolving into associative, unstructured writing indicating psychological fragmentation.
source_quote: The early entries were neat and formal and exactly what you would expect. Then, gradually, around the margins, a second voice crept in. Less structured. More associative. The sentences didn't always end. Some of them were questions that answered themselves with other questions.

subject: wax pouch contents
fact: The wax pouch contained a theological text arguing that Lolth and Zuggtmoy are the same entity, demonstrating theological contortion from a desired conclusion backward.
source_quote: It was very well-argued. It was also completely mad. It was the written record of a mind finding its way toward the conclusion that two incompatible things were secretly one thing — the kind of reasoning that starts from a desired destination and works backward.

subject: sealed orders from House Mizzrym
fact: The sealed orders from House Mizzrym were official inquiries into Ilvara’s disappearance, escalating from formal to frantic.
source_quote: Where are you? What have you been doing? Respond — kind of thing. You've gone missing. Followed by more frantic: where are you, where are you? Didn't you read the previous memo? What's up?

subject: letter from Neverlight Grove
fact: The letter from Neverlight Grove was a record of a missed political meeting, indicating Ilvara’s allegiance had shifted beyond diplomatic reach.
source_quote: A missed meeting. Political correspondence that had gone nowhere, because the person it was addressed to had gone somewhere else — somewhere a Demon Queen's influence had been a stronger pull than any political alliance.

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: House Mizzrym had been attempting to locate Ilvara and had not yet learned of her corruption or death.
source_quote: House Mizzrym would learn eventually, I supposed. We had helped with that.

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: Neverlight Grove had expected to meet Ilvara, but the meeting was missed due to her corruption and disappearance.
source_quote: A missed meeting. Political correspondence that had gone nowhere, because the person it was addressed to had gone somewhere else — somewhere a Demon Queen's influence had been a stronger pull than any political alliance.

subject: Living Serpent Head Scourge
fact: The Living Serpent Head Scourge was a weapon of remarkable craftsmanship and terrible origin, intended for display as a museum piece.
source_quote: It sounds like a great museum piece. There is a tradition, in certain temples I have visited, of displaying items that are terrible in origin and remarkable in craft, on the theory that acknowledging the craft is not the same as endorsing what the craft served.

subject: water-damaged prisoner journal
fact: The water-damaged prisoner journal contained visible handwriting in drier sections, indicating the prisoner had kept records up until they could no longer.
source_quote: The handwriting was still visible in the drier sections, the marks of a person who had kept records right up until they couldn't.

source_quote: The flask of Overbright brandy I received with considerably more personal interest.

source_quote: Confiscated prisoner belongings. Ilvara had been carrying it. Of course she had — she was exactly the sort of high priestess who would keep trophies, who would drag along evidence of her ownership of people...

subject: Thorin Giantfriend
fact: Thorin Giantfriend is referenced as the radical transparency practitioner who recovered a necromantic pearl from the heart of Ilvara’s corrupted fungal ritual site and reclaimed his own tooth, the trophy she took during his capture at Velkynvelve.
source_quote: I had the necromantic pearl in one pocket. I'd already turned over the question of what it meant — something this finished, this dense, at the core of a corrupted fungal mass that Ilvara had been using as a ritual anchor... I had the tooth back. And I had the pearl that had been buried in the heart of whatever she'd turned this place into.

subject: necromantic pearl
fact: The necromantic pearl is a smooth, dense, fist-sized object, unnaturally finished like a worked stone, found at the core of the fungal mass in the chamber once used by Ilvara as a ritual anchor, radiating a necromantic sensation akin to standing before a door to an unwanted room.
source_quote: Smooth. Dense. Fist-sized. The weight of it was wrong for something grown — too even, too finished, like a stone that had been worked by a hand that knew what it was doing. And the sensation coming off it wasn't heat or cold exactly. More like standing next to a door that opens into a room you don't want to know about. Necromantic, I decided...

subject: Ilvara's tooth
fact: Ilvara's tooth is a chip broken off during Thorin's capture at Velkynvelve, displayed by her as a trophy of power, later reclaimed by Thorin as a symbol of a settled debt.
source_quote: It was the kind of thing a person does when they want their captives to understand the power relation clearly — she'd taken my tooth. A chip broken off in the capture, displayed in her chest like a piece of evidence of what she could do... It was settled now. I had the tooth back.

subject: leather-wrapped bundle
fact: The leather-wrapped bundle contains incense cones, a silver bowl small enough to fit in one hand, and a cloth stitched with two sigils: Lolth's web woven into the eight-fold geometry of Zuggtmoy's mark, one inside the other.
source_quote: Leather-wrapped, neat in a way that the rest of the chamber wasn't. Inside: incense cones, a silver bowl small enough to fit in one hand, and a cloth that had been stitched with two sigils — Lolth's web worked into the eight-fold geometry of Zuggtmoy's mark, one woven inside the other.

subject: signet ring of House T'sarran
fact: The signet ring of House T'sarran is an unmistakable seal found on the finger of the dead mage, confirming her connection to the contract that ordered the extraction of Daz alive and unharmed.
source_quote: I found the signet ring first — House T'sarran, the seal unmistakable on the face of it.

subject: obsidian wand with captive spider
fact: The obsidian wand contains a captive spider preserved in amber at its tip, recovered from the body of the dead mage, suggesting arcane ties to the contract and possibly to Zuggtmoy’s influence.
source_quote: Then the wand: obsidian, a captive spider preserved in amber at its tip.

subject: partially burned documents
fact: The partially burned documents confirm a contract issued by House T'sarran to extract Daz alive and unharmed, arranged through intermediaries, and partially destroyed to obscure its existence.
source_quote: Then the documents. They'd been partially burned, which meant someone had tried to destroy them and hadn't quite managed it, which meant the information in them was exactly the kind of thing worth knowing... There had been a contract. Extract Daz alive and unharmed. House T'sarran behind it.

subject: Dawnbringer (sunblade)
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sunblade that refuses to be used as a ritual purification tool, asserting its purpose is to kill, not to sanctify, and is persuaded to comply only under threat of the Vaultmaster Locking Scabbard.
source_quote: "I'm not some kind of magical wizard thingy that purifies things. I am a high-quality sunblade. I kill things. I will not be treated like a religious symbol to be used and waved over corrupt..."

subject: Vaultmaster Locking Scabbard
fact: The Vaultmaster Locking Scabbard is a scabbard used by Thorin to negotiate compliance from Dawnbringer, functioning as a remarkably effective tool of restraint and persuasion.
source_quote: "Do I need to show you the scabbard again?" There was a pause... I have observed that the Vaultmaster Locking Scabbard functions as a remarkably effective negotiating tool when Dawnbringer's rhetoric outpaces its better judgment.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a male Drow apostate from Menzoberranzan, formerly imprisoned at Velkynvelve, whose mysterious value triggered a high-cost contract from House T'sarran to extract him alive, despite his lack of known lineage or consequence.
source_quote: I am not, by any meaningful measure, a person of consequence. I am a male Drow apostate from Menzoberranzan who studied magic, held private opinions that would have gotten him killed if voiced aloud, and eventually ended up in Velkynvelve's cages alongside a dwarf raised by giants and a dragonborn who doesn't talk much.

subject: Nym
fact: Nym is one of the Duskryn sisters, whose face grows more expressive when irritated, and who is skeptical of Daz’s possible noble origins, dismissing them as typical orphan fantasies.
source_quote: Nym had the kind of face that gets more expressive the more irritated she becomes, and right now she was very expressive... "Yes, yes, yes, that's what every orphan thinks. Do you have daddy issues? Do you have mommy issues? Every drow thinks there's some noble things."

subject: Kaelira
fact: Kaelira is one of the Duskryn sisters, who is still and professional, reading burned documents with focused precision, and states the most honest thing in the chamber: they are not paid to think too hard.
source_quote: Kaelira was the opposite — still and professional, reading the burned pages with the focus of someone who was paid to be good at exactly this... "Perhaps, but we're not paid to think that hard."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the individual who dealt with the platform and used acid to destroy the fungal growth infused with Zuggtmoy’s reach, collapsing it into ash.
source_quote: Behind me, Grygum was dealing with the platform... Grygum was not the sort to leave corruption breathing. He opened his mouth, and the acid came out clean and decisive, and the fungal matter that had spent months becoming something wrong collapsed into ash...

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a High Priestess who built an elevated ritual site, used fungal growth as a conduit for Zuggtmoy’s influence, collected trophies including Thorin’s tooth, and became something that served two masters and understood neither.
source_quote: Ilvara had built herself something elevated, which made a certain kind of sense — High Priestesses don't stand at floor level, they stand at the level where everyone has to look up at them... the fungal growth that had crept up the stone was still pulsing with Zuggtmoy's reach... Ilvara's madness made physical — the thing she'd built her rituals around while she was becoming something that served two masters and understood neither.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz proposes that the group jointly investigate the mystery of his value, suggesting they audit the financial and contractual records behind the contract to extract him, and offers to split any proceeds.
source_quote: "I think," I said, keeping my voice very even, "that we should investigate this together. Whatever we find — whoever is behind this, whatever they think I'm worth — we split the proceeds. Audit their books. Understand the ledger before anyone decides whether to collect the debt."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz privately acknowledges the possibility that his perceived value stems from noble blood he never earned, and finds such speculation embarrassing, preferring any answer to be more interesting than inherited status.
source_quote: I have, privately, catalogued that possibility and found it embarrassing. Whatever the answer to this question turns out to be, I prefer it to be something more interesting than inherited blood I didn't earn.

subject: chamber of Ilvara’s ritual site
fact: The chamber of Ilvara’s ritual site contains a fungal mass at its center, infused with Zuggtmoy’s reach, with a necromantic pearl embedded in its core, and evidence of her elevated platform and trophy displays.
source_quote: The fungal mass sat at the center of the chamber the way a problem sits at the center of a bad situation — obvious, unavoidable, radiating something wrong in every direction... The heart of it was still warm... The necromantic pearl... Ilvara had built herself something elevated...

subject: Velkynvelve
fact: Velkynvelve is the prison where Daz was captured and held in nets, and where Ilvara took his tooth as a trophy to establish a power dynamic between captor and captive.
source_quote: When we'd first found ourselves hanging in nets at Velkynvelve, Ilvara had made a point of collecting trophies... she'd taken my tooth.

subject: road to the surface
fact: The road to the surface is the path the party is traveling after clearing the chamber, carrying unresolved questions, recovered artifacts, and the lingering smell of scorched rot.
source_quote: Around me, the road to the surface waited. I had an unanswered question about my own identity sitting unresolved in my chest... We moved on.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran is a powerful Drow house that issued a contract to extract Daz alive and unharmed, using intermediaries and routing it through layers of opacity, indicating significant resources and reach.
source_quote: There had been a contract. Extract Daz alive and unharmed. House T'sarran behind it.

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: House Mizzrym is the noble house whose dead soldiers were found in the chamber, bearing short swords, long swords, and steel whistles, and who will never collect their pay.
source_quote: Gold, short swords, a long sword, a steel whistle. The dead soldiers of House Mizzrym would never collect their pay.

subject: Duskryn sisters
fact: The Duskryn sisters are a pair of professional Drow mercenaries hired to protect Daz, whose contrasting personalities — Nym’s expressive irritation and Kaelira’s professional stillness — shape how they interpret the mystery of his value.
source_quote: We showed the documents to Nym and Kaelira... Nym had the kind of face that gets more expressive the more irritated she becomes... Kaelira was the opposite — still and professional...

subject: Zuggtmoy's fungal growth
fact: Zuggtmoy's fungal growth is a pulsing, slow-rhythmic mass that crept up stone surfaces in Ilvara’s chamber, infused with her reach, and required acid to collapse into ash.
source_quote: the fungal growth that had crept up the stone was still pulsing with Zuggtmoy's reach, slow and rhythmic like breathing... the fungal matter that had spent months becoming something wrong collapsed into ash...

subject: Zuggtmoy
fact: Zuggtmoy is a deity whose influence is manifest in the pulsing fungal growth that infected Ilvara’s ritual chamber, and whose reach is sensed as a slow, rhythmic corruption.
source_quote: the fungal growth that had crept up the stone was still pulsing with Zuggtmoy's reach...

subject: Lolth
fact: Lolth is a deity whose web sigil was woven into the cloth stitched with Zuggtmoy’s mark, indicating a ritual synthesis of two dark powers in Ilvara’s practices.
source_quote: Lolth's web worked into the eight-fold geometry of Zuggtmoy's mark, one woven inside the other.

subject: reclamation of Thorin's tooth
fact: Thorin reclaimed his tooth, taken by Ilvara as a trophy during his capture at Velkynvelve, marking the settlement of a long-standing debt and the symbolic end of his subjugation.
source_quote: It was settled now. I had the tooth back.

subject: destruction of Zuggtmoy's fungal growth by Grygum
fact: Grygum destroyed the fungal growth infused with Zuggtmoy’s reach using acid, collapsing it into ash and eliminating a lingering corruption from the chamber.
source_quote: Grygum was not the sort to leave corruption breathing. He opened his mouth, and the acid came out clean and decisive, and the fungal matter that had spent months becoming something wrong collapsed into ash...

subject: discovery of House T'sarran contract
fact: The party discovered the partially burned documents confirming a contract from House T'sarran to extract Daz alive and unharmed, implicating him in a high-stakes political intrigue.
source_quote: Then the documents... There had been a contract. Extract Daz alive and unharmed. House T'sarran behind it.

subject: Dawnbringer's reluctant agreement to purification
fact: Dawnbringer, the sentient sunblade, reluctantly agreed to participate in a purification ritual after Thorin threatened to use the Vaultmaster Locking Scabbard, demonstrating the scabbard’s effectiveness as a diplomatic tool.
source_quote: "Do I need to show you the scabbard again?" There was a pause... "I suppose... I suppose I could do you this one. I could do this solid for you."

subject: Daz's proposal to audit the contract
fact: Daz proposed that the party jointly investigate the financial and contractual origins of the plot to extract him, offering to split any proceeds, shifting the group’s focus from suspicion to investigation.
source_quote: "I think," I said, keeping my voice very even, "that we should investigate this together... we split the proceeds. Audit their books. Understand the ledger before anyone decides whether to collect the debt."

subject: Kaelira's admission of professional detachment
fact: Kaelira stated that the party is not paid to think too hard, a moment of profound honesty that Thorin respected more than any other in the chamber.
source_quote: "Perhaps, but we're not paid to think that hard." Which was the most honest thing anyone had said in this chamber all day. I found myself respecting it more than I probably should have.

subject: chamber of the dead mage
fact: The chamber of the dead mage contains her corpse, the signet ring of House T'sarran, the obsidian wand with a captive spider in amber, and the partially burned documents confirming the contract to extract Daz.
source_quote: I found the signet ring first — House T'sarran... Then the wand: obsidian, a captive spider preserved in amber at its tip. Then the documents. They'd been partially burned...

subject: campsite on the road to the surface
fact: The campsite on the road to the surface is where Daz reflects on his identity, the Duskryn sisters debate his possible nobility, and the party debates the use of Dawnbringer in ritual purification.
source_quote: The question had been sitting in the middle of our camp like a stone none of us wanted to trip over... Around me, the road to the surface waited...

subject: Thorin Giantfriend
fact: Thorin Giantfriend is a man of radical transparency who chooses silence when speech adds nothing to the next ten seconds, and who carries the necromantic pearl and his reclaimed tooth as symbols of a journey from captivity to agency.
source_quote: Thorin Giantfriend, radical transparency, except when the thing being said wouldn't add anything to the next ten seconds... I didn't say any of that out loud.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a Drow who refuses to accept easy narratives about his identity, preferring to pursue truth through investigation rather than fantasy, and whose quiet dignity contrasts with the skepticism of others.
source_quote: So then maybe there's more to me than meets the eye?... Which was, I thought, the most restrained thing he could possibly have said in that moment.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced as the one who stopped counting steps around the third hour of climbing because counting had started to feel like superstition, like measuring distance against the possibility of failure.
source_quote: I had stopped counting the steps somewhere around the third hour of climbing — not because I lost track, but because counting had started to feel like superstition, like I was measuring the distance against the possibility of failure.

subject: tunnel mouth
fact: The tunnel mouth opened like a held breath finally released, and the air thinned in a way that had nothing to do with depth; it simply became something else, something with weather in it.
source_quote: The tunnel mouth opened like a held breath finally released. The air changed first. It thinned in a way that had nothing to do with depth; it simply became something else. Something with weather in it.

subject: Overbright
fact: The Overbright was a concept Zalthir had been carrying through Velkynvelve and Gracklstugh and the Darklake and Blingdenstone like a stone in a pocket, something reached for when the tunnels pressed too close.
source_quote: The Overbright was a concept I had been carrying through Velkynvelve and Gracklstugh and the Darklake and Blingdenstone like a stone in a pocket, something I reached for when the tunnels pressed too close.

subject: Overbright
fact: The light that came through the tunnel mouth was not like Dawnbringer's light, not like faerie fire or bioluminescence, but a light that simply *was*, filling everything from every direction at once.
source_quote: The light that came through the tunnel mouth was not like Dawnbringer's light, not like faerie fire or bioluminescence or any of the things we had been navigating by for however many months it had been — It was not a light that came from a source. It was a light that simply *was*, filling everything from every direction at once.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin emerged first, as he always led from the front, always had, it was as close to instinct as that dwarf ever got.
source_quote: Thorin first, which was correct — he always led from the front, always had, it was as close to instinct as that dwarf ever got.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum emerged next, blinking with something that looked less like discomfort and more like relief, the earnest half-orc having what appeared to be a genuine spiritual moment with direct sunlight.
source_quote: Grygum next, blinking with something that looked less like discomfort and more like relief, the earnest half-orc having what appeared to be a genuine spiritual moment with direct sunlight.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz came through last, the way Daz always came through last, already observing before he was fully present, already composing the analysis before his feet had cleared the threshold.
source_quote: Daz came through last, the way Daz always came through last, already observing before he was fully present, already composing the analysis before his feet had cleared the threshold.

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth was part of the moltley crew that followed, having survived the journey through the Underdark.
source_quote: The rest of our moltley crew followed, Eldeth, Spiderbait, and the rest of the folks who had survived this journey.

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait was part of the moltley crew that followed, having survived the journey through the Underdark.
source_quote: The rest of our moltley crew followed, Eldeth, Spiderbait, and the rest of the folks who had survived this journey.

subject: Drow cloak
fact: Drow cloaks disintegrated in the sunlight, and Zalthir put his cloak in a bag.
source_quote: I knew that Drow cloaks disintegrated in the sunlight. I put my cloak in a bag.

subject: Brother Quellin
fact: Brother Quellin was possibly the one who taught the class on material impermanence — the transience of tools, the attachment to implements, something about a bowl and an empty hand.
source_quote: I think it was Brother Quellin, or possibly the tall one whose name I never quite caught, the one who always had chalk dust on his robe. The transience of tools. The attachment to implements. Something about a bowl and an empty hand.

subject: bag of holding
fact: Grygum had opened the bag of holding just enough, allowing Glabbagool to peer out.
source_quote: Grygum had opened the bag of holding just enough, and Glabbagool — our companion, our gelatinous ward who was now a grey ooze — had peered out.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool was our companion, our gelatinous ward who was now a grey ooze, the most improbable relationship any of us had formed in the Underdark.
source_quote: Glabbagool — our companion, our gelatinous ward who was now a grey ooze, the most improbable relationship any of us had formed in the Underdark, which was saying something given the competition.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool had not been in sunlight before, and his eyes — whatever they were structurally — were wide and present and sweeping across the surface world with an attention that made Zalthir’s response to the Overbright seem measured.
source_quote: He had not been in sunlight before. None of us were entirely sure what Glabbagool's eyes were, from a structural standpoint, but they were wide and present and sweeping across the surface world with an attention that made my own response to the Overbright seem, by comparison, measured.

subject: Stonespeaker Crystal
fact: The Stonespeaker Crystal was Daz's.
source_quote: The Stonespeaker Crystal was Daz's.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was suspected of already drafting a journal entry while standing in the Overbright.
source_quote: Daz was, I suspected, already drafting a journal entry.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep, the Great Library, was the proposed destination for research into House T'sarran and Jimjar's disappearance and the various cutouts and hired Duskryns pointing at Daz's own history.
source_quote: The conclusion — Candlekeep, the Great Library, research into House T'sarran and Jimjar's disappearance and whatever the various cutouts and hired Duskryns were ultimately pointing at regarding Daz's own history — was reasonable.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin was thinking about Dawnbringer — what it had been through, months of darkness, a blade whose nature was radiance forced to endure the complete absence of the thing it was built to carry.
source_quote: Thorin, characteristically, was thinking about Dawnbringer. Not what to do with it; he would never give it up, and the sword would never go quietly. But what it had been through. Months of darkness, months of the deep, a blade whose nature was radiance forced to endure the complete absence of the thing it was built to carry.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin had mentioned a specialist — the phrase *sword whisperer* had come up, delivered with dwarvish seriousness that meant he believed this person existed and should be found.
source_quote: He had mentioned something about a specialist — the phrase *sword whisperer* had come up, delivered with the particular dwarvish seriousness that Thorin applied to things he actually cared about, which meant he believed this person existed and should be found.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum had pamphlets on his mind — he would look up the lore of Bahamut, pick up pamphlets, and be genuinely delighted by the availability of pamphlets.
source_quote: Grygum had pamphlets on his mind. This was entirely consistent. Grygum was the only one among us who had accumulated a list of things he wanted to read, and Candlekeep was going to be, for him, something between research and pilgrimage. He would look up the lore of Bahamut. He would pick up pamphlets. He would be genuinely delighted by the availability of pamphlets.

subject: gold
fact: The group had more gold than they had started with — which was not saying much, given that they had started with nothing.
source_quote: We had more of it than we had started with — which was not saying much, given that we had started with nothing.

subject: adventuring gear
fact: The group agreed on investing the gold in adventuring gear, because gear reduced the consequences of danger, and business ventures required infrastructure and stability they did not have.
source_quote: The logic for adventuring gear was simple enough that even I could lay it out without needing a meeting: we were people who went into danger. Gear reduced the consequences of danger. Business ventures required infrastructure we did not have, stability we had not earned, and a calendar that the demon lord situation was unlikely to respect. We agreed on the gear.

subject: surface world
fact: Zalthir stood at the entrance to the surface world, squinting at a sky that went farther than anything he had navigated in months, and thought: this is where we were going.
source_quote: I stood at the entrance to the surface world, squinting at a sky that went farther than anything I had navigated in months, and I thought: this is where we were going.

subject: emergence into the Overbright
fact: The group stood in the Overbright for a while, longer than was probably necessary from a tactical standpoint, and nobody suggested moving immediately — unusual for a group that treated stillness as the thing you did when stillness was the only remaining option.
source_quote: We stood in the Overbright for a while, longer than was probably necessary from a tactical standpoint, and nobody suggested moving immediately. That was unusual. We were a group that moved quickly, that had learned to move quickly, that treated stillness as the thing you did when stillness was the only remaining option.

subject: arrival at the surface
fact: The group had made it to the surface, and now there was everything else.
source_quote: We had made it. Now there was everything else.
